column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says images for the Baals; BSB says images of the Baals.
The Hebrew names the valley of the son of Hinnom and explicitly says he burned his sons; BSB uses Hinnom and sacrificed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves Ahaz unnamed and uses plural agents striking and taking captives after the king of Aram is named; BSB names Ahaz and links singular who to the king.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the house; BSB specifies the palace.
The Hebrew calls the captors sons of Israel and the captives their brothers; BSB uses Israelites and kinsmen.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the intended slaves sons of Judah and Jerusalem; BSB specifies men and women.
The Hebrew calls the captives their brothers rather than kinsmen.
The Hebrew calls the Ephraimites sons of Ephraim and those returning coming from the army.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they anointed them without an explicit wounds noun; BSB supplies their wounds.
The Hebrew has kings of Assyria in the plural; BSB has the king in the singular.
Close to the Hebrew.
The dependent towns are called daughters and attached separately to Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo.
The Hebrew emphasizes unfaithfulness by repeating the same root.
The Hebrew leaves Ahaz unnamed and joins distressing him and not strengthening him with and.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the gods of Damascus as striking him; BSB makes Damascus the defeating subject and names Ahaz at the end.
The Hebrew repeats the articles of God’s house and says every corner, without a separate street noun.
The Hebrew repeats city to distribute the statement; BSB uses every city.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Ahaz’s name.
The Hebrew has unnamed plural agents burying and not bringing him to the tombs; BSB makes both passive.
